pipeline_mapping: **the soil-mechanics force model behind our `Drilling / excavation energy` row (operational_costs.csv, 200 Wh/kg median)**: analytical drawbar-force model for digging lunar regolith from standard soil-strength parameters — the physics that converts loose-vs-consolidated into a force/energy split. JSC-1a simulant measured in-paper: density **1680 kg/m3**, cohesion **c=170 N/m2** (low, as expected for lunar surface soil), internal friction angle **phi=35 deg**, specific gravity 2.85; tool params w=1 m, d up to 1 m, v=0.1-1.63 m/s, g_moon. Key finding: required force is STRONGLY cohesion-dependent (lowest for cohesionless soil, highest for very cohesive) — the model basis for our row's 'loose regolith ≲50 Wh/kg / consolidated rock ≳500' split; pairs with metzger_zacny_2020 (thermal side of drilling) and just_2019 (measured specific-energy table, still open_not_pulled).

pipeline_mapping: the NASA Glenn APEX (Advanced Planetary Excavator) test facility: electrically-driven linear-actuator digger on 325 VDC/100 A bus; bucket 21.6 cm wide x 15,600 cm3 volume, 30 deg blade angle; load cell **1300 N (Fx,Fy) / 3900 N (Fz)**, torque ±203 N-m, uncertainty ≤2%; platform scale to 2224 N; GRC-3B soil bin (1587 kg fill). Method: measure power+forces in air AND simulant with identical motion profile, subtract tare → net excavation power. This is the measurement chain that produces per-test Wh/kg values for loose regolith — the institutional basis our 200 Wh/kg median row assumes.
